title: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank Ltd - 543942 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Utkarsh SFB Q2 FY27 PPoP rose to INR85 crores and net loss narrowed to INR70 crores, with credit cost at 3.3% and GNPA at 5.9%.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 PPoP of INR85 crores, up 34% sequentially from Q1 and up from an operating loss of INR3 crores in Q2 FY26. Net loss was INR70 crores in Q2 and INR104 crores in H1, down about 80% YoY in Q2. Q2 provisions rose to INR166 crores from INR109 crores in Q1, but management said Q1 included a CGFMU credit of INR75 crores and an ARC-related credit of INR65 crores, so the underlying comparison is better. Gross loan portfolio grew 7.5% YoY and 2.3% QoQ, while disbursements grew 52% in H1; management still guided to 25-30% FY28 loan growth and 15% ROE in FY28.

financial_highlights.change: +34% QoQ; vs operating loss of INR3 crores in Q2 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Credit cost (Q2 FY27, as per Q&A)
financial_highlights.change: Q1 FY27 was 2.3%; 5.1% in Q1 excluding CGFMU and ARC credits

financial_highlights.value: ~INR175 crores in Q2 FY27 (management also cited INR239 crores gross in Q&A)
financial_highlights.change: vs ~INR415 crores in Q2 FY26; H1 INR300 crores vs ~INR810 crores
CASA plus retail term deposit ratio 82% vs 78% a year ago

segments.name: Micro banking (JLG/MBBL)
segments.commentary: JLG share of gross loans fell to 24% (26% incl. BC JLG) from 88% in March 2020. MBBL grew 146% YoY and 15% QoQ, now 35% of micro banking; SMA pool fell to 1.7% from 4.9% in Sep 2025. JLG disbursements grew 2% in H1.

segments.name: Secured lending
segments.commentary: Secured share rose to 52% of gross loans from 47% a year ago. MSME portfolio was INR4,489 crores (+8% YoY); housing INR984 crores (+4% YoY); BBG grew 38% YoY. Management said H1 MSME and housing disbursement slowdown was tied to an August slowdown from the new CBS launch.

segments.name: Non-JLG disbursements
segments.commentary: Non-JLG disbursements grew 94% in H1 FY27; Q2 non-MFI disbursements grew 87% YoY. Disbursement yields: retail MSME ~13%, housing ~11%, CV/CE ~12.2%, wholesale ~10.9-11%, personal loan ~16%, gold ~12%.

segments.name: CV/CE (wheels)
segments.commentary: Wheels slippages fell from ~INR44 crores to ~INR27 crores in each of the last two quarters, then ~INR30 crores in Q2. Used vehicles are ~30% of disbursements; management said loans from April 2025 onward show GNPA below 1%.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan portfolio is around INR400 crores-plus; expansion via a digital loan origination system.

guidance_outlook: FY27 loan book growth of 25-30%, which management reiterated after H1 growth of 7.5% YoY; management said H2 disbursements would need to be substantially higher.
FY28 targets: NIM around 8%, ROE around 15%, secured lending around 55% of the portfolio.
ROE expected to exit FY27 in the double digits (Q4 FY27), with a return to profitability in FY27.
Cost-to-income ratio targeted at around 70-75% by FY27 exit and 60-65% sustainable in FY28.
Credit costs expected to decline in Q3 and Q4 FY27; management said provisioning is on a declining trajectory.
Headcount expected to remain in roughly the same range (+/-100-200) over the next six months, with any increase in FOS roles.
Equity raise not planned in the current year; INR200 crores Tier 2 raise planned this quarter. Reverse merger of Utkarsh CoreInvest into the bank is awaiting the NCLT hearing on November 19, 2026.
capex_capacity: Branch network is around 1,100 (about 780 MFI and 330 general banking branches). No new branches opened in the last 18+ months; management said branch expansion cost is zero.
New core banking system launched in Q2 FY27, which caused a slowdown in August disbursements.
Utkarsh 2.0 technology transformation is ongoing; retail lending is fully on LOS, and rule engine, Perfios and Saverisk are used internally.
Employee headcount is about 18,300, down close to 1,100 YoY.
Collection workforce for JLG and MBBL exceeds 1,400 personnel; a specialized call centre for overdue accounts has been set up.
demand_pricing: Disbursements grew 52% YoY in H1 FY27 (Q2 +55%; non-MFI +87% in Q2). Q4 FY26 disbursements grew 30%, Q1 FY27 50%.
Management said the NIM rise (5.1% to 6.3%) reflects improving yields, lower funding cost and higher processing fees from disbursements.
Around 50% of the portfolio is floating rate; ~80% of deposits are term deposits, so repricing of higher rates will be gradual. Market borrowing is nil.
CGFMU guarantee window is closed for fresh cover pending the government's next phase. Management has accrued the 1% guarantee fee on eligible disbursements.
Collection efficiency in the JLG X-bucket was 99.6% in Q2 vs 98.6% a year earlier. October Maharashtra collection (under 5% of the book) was about 98.83%, versus ~99.5% average previously.

qa_highlights.question: Why did provisions rise from INR109 crores in Q1 to INR166 crores in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 included a CGFMU credit of ~INR75 crores and an ARC sale benefit of ~INR65 crores. Adding these back, Q1 provisions would have been ~INR240-250 crores, so Q2 is an improvement.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sequential uptick in slippages to INR239 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said MB contributed INR66 crores and non-MB INR173 crores (CV/CE INR30 crores, MSME INR64 crores, WSL INR33 crores). Recoveries from WSL were INR8 crores. Management said drought and West Asia factors did not affect the NPA trend.

qa_highlights.question: Will the CGFMU-covered book and claims be recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: Covered book is about INR6,500 crores as of Sep 30, 2026, of which INR209 crores is NPA. The first claim of around INR80 crores plus has been submitted and is under process.

qa_highlights.question: What are the NIM and cost of funds outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost of funds should stay controlled because of term-deposit repricing lags and the floating-rate share, and that higher costs can be passed through. The path to 8% NIM relies on this plus the secured mix.

qa_highlights.question: Is an equity raise planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no immediate equity plan and equity is not expected this year. Capital adequacy is 17%, and INR200 crores of Tier 2 is planned in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the branch throughput low and is FY27 loan growth realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was held back by legacy challenges and ARC transfers. It expects 25-30% growth in FY27 and said disbursement momentum is returning, with H2 disbursements expected to be higher.

risks_watch: Q2 provisioning rose to INR166 crores QoQ; management says clean-up of legacy micro-banking stress is nearly complete, but CV/CE and MSME slippages remain elevated.
CGFMU guarantee cover lapses after March 2026 and the window is closed for new disbursements until the next phase is approved; premium costs will hit P&L.
Repricing of term deposits and possible repo-rate hikes could pressure cost of funds and the 8% NIM target.
Growth in MSME, CV and housing was weak in H1 and management attributed it partly to the CBS launch; secured disbursement momentum needs to show in Q3.
Segment-wise GNPA and NNPA disclosure requested by analysts was not given; management committed to add it.
NCLT hearing for the reverse merger of Utkarsh CoreInvest on November 19, 2026.
key_quotes: Albeit our growth has been a little slow but steady, and the same is ready to pick pace now.
So, our plan is to raise INR200 crores Tier 2 capital during this quarter, based on market conditions.
Point taken, point taken. We'll ensure that part. Sorry, missed it, but we'll ensure that part.
So, the repricing of fixed deposits will take some time, even if the rates go up tomorrow because we are not dependent on any market borrowing.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on collections, fresh slippages, funding costs and the ROE trajectory, while repeatedly explaining away the Q2 provision increase by adding back Q1 CGFMU and ARC credits. It was cautious on growth, saying growth was "a little slow" and that disbursements in August slowed because of the CBS launch, and it was evasive on segment-wise GNPA/NNPA and Stage 1/Stage 2 coverage, which it did not provide.

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 loan book growth of 25-30% (25%+) against only 7.5% YoY growth in H1, with H2 disbursements needing to be substantially higher; disbursements grew 52% in H1 and the bank guides ROE exiting FY27 in double digits, but no specific new capacity, orders or contracts were quantified behind the growth guidance, so backing is vague.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM rose to 6.3% from 5.1% a year ago on better yields, lower cost of funds (7.4%, down ~50 bps YoY) and processing fees; management targets ~8% NIM in FY28, though ~80% term deposits mean repricing is gradual.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new branches in the last 18+ months on a ~1,100 branch network, headcount flat at ~18,300 (down ~1,100 YoY), and management says branch expansion cost is zero; capacity growth is not the story.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Disbursements grew 52% in H1 FY27 (Q2 +55%, non-MFI +87%), but loan book grew only 7.5% YoY, so management needs H2 disbursements substantially higher to hit 25-30% FY27 growth.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed as a need; the bank is on a new CBS and LOS platform and has no utilisation-driven capacity constraint, with capital adequacy at 17% and no equity raise planned this year.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 loan growth at 25-30% and FY28 ROE at ~15% despite H1 growth of 7.5% YoY, so no upgrade is signalled and the bar is high.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 loan growth of 25%+ needs a big H2 step-up from 7.5% YoY in H1, and Q2 provisions rose to INR166 crores from INR109 crores; CGFMU cover has lapsed for new disbursements, and CV/CE and MSME slippages remain elevated.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Gold loan expansion via a digital loan origination system (gold book ~INR400 crores-plus) and a Tier 2 INR200 crores raise in Q3 are discussed, but no specific new product launch date was given.

rows.label: Cost-to-income falls to 70-75% by FY27 exit, 60-65% in FY28
rows.why: Cost-to-income improved to 84% from ~110% in Q3 FY26 with headcount flat and a 1,400+ collection workforce; management guides to 70-75% by FY27 exit.

rows.label: Credit costs decline and return to profitability
rows.why: Credit cost was 3.3% in Q2 (5.1% in Q1 excluding CGFMU and ARC credits) and management expects declines in Q3 and Q4 FY27, with ROE exiting FY27 in double digits.

rows.label: Reverse merger of Utkarsh CoreInvest into the bank
rows.why: The merger is awaiting the NCLT hearing on November 19, 2026, and its outcome is not yet known.

tone.note: Management was confident on collections, slippages, funding costs and the ROE path, but cautious on growth (called it 'a little slow') and evasive on segment GNPA/NNPA and Stage 2 coverage, while analysts pressed on the Q2 provision rise and on the credibility of 25-30% FY27 growth.
